emergency.notes: Police: 110. Fire and Ambulance: 119. English-speaking operators available via 0800-024-111 (foreigner assistance hotline). Tourist Police in Taipei: +886-2-2556-6007.

travelAdvisory.summary: Exercise normal precautions in Taiwan. Taiwan is one of the safest destinations in Asia. Violent crime is rare. The main risks are natural disasters including earthquakes and typhoons. Cross-strait tensions with China exist but do not typically affect daily life.

travelAdvisoryUK.summary: Taiwan is generally a safe destination. Be prepared for earthquakes and typhoons. Monitor weather warnings and follow advice from local authorities during typhoon season.

healthcare.systemType: Excellent universal healthcare (NHI system). Tourists pay out of pocket — very affordable by international standards.
healthcare.costForTourists: Clinic visit $5-30 USD. Hospital emergency visit $30-150. Hospital admission $100-400/night. Medical care is affordable and high quality. Dental care is particularly good value.
healthcare.pharmacyAccess: 7-Eleven-style pharmacies and dedicated pharmacies everywhere. English-speaking pharmacists in cities. Most common medications available without prescription.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Taiwan's medical system is world-class with excellent hospital networks. National Taiwan University Hospital, Taipei Veterans General, and MacKay Memorial Hospital all have international patient services. English widely spoken at major hospitals.
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: Travel insurance recommended as tourists pay out of pocket. Costs are very affordable by Western standards but insurance provides peace of mind for major events.

controlledSubstances.note: Carry original prescription with translation to Chinese if possible. Declare at customs.
Strictly illegal. Taiwan has severe drug penalties including long prison sentences. Zero tolerance.
Some ADHD medications classified as controlled substances in Taiwan. Carry prescription and doctor's letter. Bring sufficient supply from home.

medications.generalAdvice: Taiwan's medical care is excellent and affordable. Bring adequate supplies of prescription medications. Carry all medications in original packaging with English prescriptions.

scams.name: Night market overcharging
scams.description: Some night market vendors charge higher prices to obviously foreign tourists. Prices may not be displayed.
scams.avoidance: Look for posted prices before ordering. Learn approximate costs for common foods. Most vendors are honest — overcharging is relatively rare.

scams.name: Fake taxi or rideshare at tourist sites
scams.description: Unofficial drivers at popular tourist locations claim to offer better rates than legitimate taxis or ride-hailing apps.
scams.avoidance: Use Taiwan Taxi app (台灣大車隊), LINE Taxi, or Uber for metered fares. Official taxis are metered and generally honest.

scams.name: Temple fortune telling scam
scams.description: Fortune tellers near popular temples pressure tourists into expensive readings and follow-up 'spiritual services' with escalating costs.
scams.avoidance: Legitimate temple fortune telling is inexpensive or donation-based. Be wary of any fortune teller who quotes high prices or suggests ongoing expensive ceremonies.

scams.name: Counterfeit goods at markets
scams.description: Counterfeit branded goods (shoes, bags, electronics) are sold at markets, sometimes presented as genuine discounted items.
scams.avoidance: Do not expect genuine branded goods at market prices. Customs in your home country may confiscate counterfeits.

connectivity.simOptions: Tourist SIMs (Chunghwa Telecom, Taiwan Mobile, Far EasTone) at Taoyuan Airport arrivals. 5-day to 30-day packages $5-20 with 3-5GB or unlimited data. eSIM via Airalo or direct from carriers.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Excellent free WiFi nationwide through iTaiwan (government network at airports, stations, public buildings). Most cafes, restaurants, and accommodation offer free WiFi.
connectivity.bestOption: Tourist SIM from Taoyuan Airport for easiest setup. iTaiwan WiFi registration available at airport for free backup access.

cultural.tipping: Not expected or customary in Taiwan. Tipping may cause confusion or mild embarrassment. High-end hotels may have a 10% service charge added to bills. No tipping needed for taxis, restaurants, or guides.
cultural.dressCode: Casual dress widely acceptable. Modest clothing when visiting temples. Remove shoes before entering many businesses, homes, and some temples.
cultural.greetings: Standard greeting is a slight bow or nod. Handshakes common in business settings. First names used in casual contexts. Business cards exchanged with both hands — receive with respect and look at it before putting away.
taboos: Sticking chopsticks upright in a bowl of rice (funeral ritual symbolism)
Passing food chopstick to chopstick (associated with funeral rites)
Writing names in red ink (associated with death)
Giving clocks or umbrellas as gifts (symbolizes death and separation in Mandarin)
The number 4 is considered unlucky (sounds like 'death' in Mandarin)
Pointing with index finger (use open hand instead)
cultural.haggling: Not typical in most settings. Fixed prices in shops, restaurants, and convenience stores. Some bargaining possible at traditional markets and for bulk purchases.

safety.lgbtSafety: Taiwan is the most LGBTQ+-friendly country in Asia. Same-sex marriage has been legal since 2019. Taipei Pride is the largest in Asia. LGBTQ+ visitors are welcome and accepted in cities and tourist areas.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Excellent. Taiwan is one of the safest countries in the world for solo female travelers. Violent crime is extremely rare. Night market culture means cities are lively and safe until late.
safety.notes: Taiwan is one of the safest travel destinations in Asia. The main risks are natural disasters (earthquakes are common but usually minor). Cross-strait tensions with China are a background geopolitical concern but do not affect daily tourist activities.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US, UK, EU, Australia, Canada, Japan, South Korea and many others receive visa-free entry for 90 days. Check boca.gov.tw for current list.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: October-November and March-May for mild weather. Avoid July-September (typhoon season). Lunar New Year (Jan/Feb) is festive but businesses close. Lantern Festival in February is spectacular.

hospitals.name: National Taiwan University Hospital
hospitals.address: 7 Chung Shan S. Road, Zhongzheng District, Taipei
hospitals.notes: Premier hospital in Taiwan. Excellent emergency and specialist care. International patient services available.

hospitals.name: MacKay Memorial Hospital
hospitals.address: 92 Zhongshan N. Road Sec. 2, Zhongshan District, Taipei
hospitals.notes: Highly recommended for foreign visitors. Long tradition of treating international patients. Good English services.

hospitals.name: Kaohsiung Chang Gung Memorial Hospital
hospitals.notes: Major hospital serving southern Taiwan. International patient services available.

immediate: Drop, cover, and hold on — get under a desk or sturdy table and hold on
Stay away from windows, exterior walls, and heavy shelving
If outdoors, move to open area away from buildings, trees, and power lines
Do not use elevators after shaking stops
Expect aftershocks — stay alert and ready to take cover again
after: Check for gas leaks and structural damage before re-entering buildings
Follow Taiwan's National Fire Agency alerts and local authority instructions
Register safety status with AIT if assistance needed
Monitor 1991 hotline (disaster response) for updates in Chinese/English
resources: Central Weather Bureau seismic data: www.cwb.gov.tw

immediate: Monitor Central Weather Bureau typhoon warnings (English available at cwb.gov.tw)
When sea warning issued: secure loose outdoor items, stock 3 days of water and food
When land warning issued: stay indoors, away from windows
If evacuation ordered, follow government instructions and leave immediately
Do not attempt to travel during active typhoon — wait for official all-clear
after: Watch for flash floods and landslides which often follow typhoons
Do not approach swollen rivers or coastal areas immediately after typhoon
Check road conditions before traveling in mountain or coastal areas
Report damage to local government and insurance
resources: Central Weather Bureau typhoon forecast: www.cwb.gov.tw
